title: OCR evaluation dataset manifest
description: Declares a private, de-identified OCR ground-truth dataset. The manifest is the ONLY authority on what each fixture is: document type, language, capture style and handwriting are declared by a human who looked at the page, never inferred from OCR output or from engine confidence. Fixture files and transcripts live outside version control; this manifest records their hashes so a silent substitution fails closed.

schema_version.description: Frozen at 2. A different value must fail closed rather than be coerced. VERSION 1 IS REFUSED, NOT MIGRATED: v2 made document_family, split, field and occurrence_index required, and a v1 manifest carries none of them. Defaulting them would produce a dataset with no train/holdout separation and no field annotation -- which still scores, and scores meaninglessly. There is no automatic migration; a v1 manifest must be re-annotated, because the missing information is a human judgement about the documents and cannot be inferred from the file.

dataset_id.description: Stable identifier for this dataset revision. Appears in reports so a number can be traced to the exact corpus that produced it.

created_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of manifest creation.

notes.description: Free text about provenance or scope. MUST NOT contain document text, names or any other identifier drawn from the fixtures.

de_identified.description: Dataset-level de-identification attestation. Required: these are real legal documents, and the whole dataset is disqualified if any page still carries a living person's identifiers.

confirmed.description: Must be literally true. Absent or false fails closed — there is no 'probably de-identified'.

confirmed_by.description: Role or initials of the human who verified it. Not an email address.

method.description: How identifiers were removed or replaced (e.g. 'names and CNICs replaced with consistent synthetic values before scanning').

consent.description: Permission to use these documents for evaluation. Separate from de-identification: a de-identified document may still be one we were never permitted to retain.

basis.description: Why we may hold and process these (e.g. 'synthetic documents authored for evaluation', 'written consent from the client, reference on file').

expires_utc.description: When permission lapses, if it does. A run after this date must fail closed.

fixtures.description: The pages. A real accuracy dataset is expected to hold 30-50 representative pages; the schema does not enforce that, because enforcing a count would tempt padding with unrepresentative pages to reach it.

fixture_id.description: Unique within the manifest. Used in reports INSTEAD of the filename, because filenames of real legal documents are themselves identifying.

path.description: Path to the fixture, RELATIVE to the manifest's own directory. Absolute paths and any '..' segment are rejected by the loader: a manifest must not be able to reach outside the dataset directory.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex digest of the fixture bytes. Verified on every run so a re-scanned or re-compressed file cannot silently change what a historical score meant.

language.description: Language of the page CONTENT, declared by a human reader.

script_style.description: Urdu legal documents appear in both Naskh and Nastaliq, and Tesseract handles them very differently. Recording it is what makes a bad aggregate score diagnosable instead of merely bad.

capture.description: searchable = already has a text layer (OCR should not be needed); scanned = flatbed/MFP image; photograph = camera, with the lighting and perspective that implies.

writing.description: Declared by a human. NEVER derived from OCR confidence.

handwriting_policy.description: REQUIRED whenever writing is 'handwritten' or 'mixed'. Handwriting is out of scope until separately evaluated; the harness skips these fixtures by policy and counts them, rather than scoring them and dragging an aggregate down for a capability never claimed.

rotation.description: Category, not degrees. Degrees imply a measurement precision a human eyeballing a scan does not have.

expected_page_count.description: Checked against what the reader reports. A mismatch means the file is not the document the manifest describes, and fails that fixture closed.

transcript_path.description: Path to the manually verified UTF-8 ground-truth transcript, relative to the manifest directory. Same containment rules as `path`. A missing transcript fails that fixture closed — it can never be treated as an empty expected string, which would score any output as pure insertion error.

transcript_sha256.description: Optional but recommended: pins the ground truth as firmly as the input.

critical_tokens.description: Strings whose EXACT reproduction matters more than the aggregate: names, dates, amounts, section numbers. A 2% CER that lands on 'PPC 302' is not the same failure as one spread over prose. May be empty, but the key must be present, so 'no critical tokens' is a decision rather than an omission.

value.description: The exact expected string. MUST already be de-identified: this value IS quoted in failure output, so a real name here would leak into every report.

field.description: Which semantic slot this value fills: fine_amount, imprisonment_years, section_number, order_date, respondent_name. Required because token PRESENCE does not establish correctness -- 'fine 1000 imprisonment 3' and 'fine 3 imprisonment 1000' contain the same tokens and mean opposite things. Scoring field accuracy is impossible without this.

occurrence_index.description: 0-based index of this occurrence of the SAME field on the page, in reading order. A judgment listing three fines needs each bound to its own slot.

context_before.description: Verbatim reference text immediately preceding the value, used to locate it in a hypothesis. This is what makes field binding checkable without a layout model.

context_after.description: Verbatim reference text immediately following the value.

de_identified.description: Per-fixture confirmation. The dataset-level attestation covers intent; this one is ticked per page, because de-identification fails one page at a time.

synthetic.description: True for fixtures generated to exercise harness mechanics. Any run containing a synthetic fixture is reported as HARNESS_TEST_ONLY_NOT_ACCURACY_EVIDENCE in full — the label is never applied per-fixture, because a mixed run's aggregate would otherwise read as accuracy evidence.

notes.description: Human notes. MUST NOT contain document text beyond the declared critical tokens.

document_family.description: Documents sharing layout, typeface, scanner or issuing office belong to ONE family. The train/holdout split is applied per family, never per page or per fixture: pages from one document share almost everything that makes OCR easy or hard, so splitting below family level leaks the holdout into tuning and inflates the score.

split.description: Which side of the tuning/holdout separation this fixture sits on. Every fixture in a document_family MUST carry the same value; a family split across both sides is a leak and fails the manifest closed.

then.description: Handwriting must be declared unsupported_by_policy explicitly.
